$description: The checkable rules, as data. Every condition in contract.md has exactly one machine-readable entry here and is evaluated in exactly one place (check.mjs). Reasoning for any of these lives in decisions.md; measured results live in outcomes.md. Nothing here restates a value that a token file already holds.

type_bounds.$description: F3. Bounds the DTOS 2025.10 value schemas impose, held here rather than as literals in check.mjs, so the checker states no number of its own. Source: schemas/src/2025.10/format/values/*.json.

manifest.$description: B4, B5. Four emitted homes now: the token CSS, the compiled recipe CSS, and the typed module with its declarations (the package the portfolio and Metis bind); no second copy to drift from. It stamps the manifest version on its first line (B5, extracted with the pattern below), and B4 rebuilds the CSS from source in memory and byte-compares the committed file to it, so a source edit that was never rebuilt cannot pass. The version's single home is packages/ame-tokens/ame.json.

naming.$description: N1. Every path segment. Lowercase, digits, single hyphen or underscore as separator. DTOS additionally forbids '.', '{', '}' and a leading '$' in any name; F5 checks those.

synonyms.$description: N2. One word per concept, across token paths and the repo's own exported symbols (Deissenboeck & Pizka's name-to-concept bijection; STANDARD.md N3). Each pair names the canonical word for a concept and the deprecated synonym that must not enter a new identifier. An identifier is tokenized on '-', '_', '.', '/' and camelCase boundaries; a deprecated word appearing as one of those tokens fails N2 unless the whole identifier is listed in `waived`. Vendored code (components/ui) is out of scope: its names are the upstream's call, not this repo's, the same exemption R-8 gives vendored files. Scope note: this reads identifiers, not Tailwind class strings or CSS custom-property call sites, so a `bg-*` utility class is untouched.
synonyms.waived_because: Each waived name is a bound token deliverable: a rename is a consumer migration, global-or-nothing (DECISIONS R-1's boundary on CSS custom-property renames), so the abbreviation stays until a dedicated migration order. The two concepts already carry both spellings in the tree, background/bg and button/btn, and the canonical is the fuller word the semantic role home and the component symbols already use. N2 blocks a third occurrence from landing, which is what the ratchet is for.

layering.$description: L1 to L3. A layer may reference only the layers listed. literalTypes lists the $types a layer may state outright rather than reference.

recipe.$description: L4. A recipe token is the value one slot of one component takes. It references the tiers below it, exactly as a component token does, and may state a dimension or number literal for a measure with no shared scale.

contrast.$description: C1 to C10, foreground over background, WCAG 2.2 relative-luminance ratio computed from the resolved token values. A translucent foreground is composited over its background before measuring. min 4.5 is AA for normal text; 7 is AAA; 3 is AA for large text (over 24px, WCAG 1.4.3) and for non-text contrast (WCAG 1.4.11: focus indicators, graphical objects, the boundaries of a control). The minimum is per pair, so a pair states the threshold its own role actually carries rather than inheriting one. Each theme-following reading pair (a foreground with an -on-dark counterpart, over a ground listed in darkGround) is evaluated a second time as it resolves under [data-theme=dark], and checked against the same min (reported Cn-dark). The dark twin is derived from the -on-dark suffix and darkGround, so a new reading pair is covered in both themes without a second row. This closes the gap where C1's 7:1 held only the light half. Every pair declares a role (reading, fixed, chrome, or backdrop); a pair with no role fails, so a new row cannot default to unclassified and skip the cross silently. A role:reading pair must produce a twin; a missing or misspelled -on-dark sibling fails the check rather than passing quietly.

pairs.$description: The focus indicator against the paper page. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of a focus ring, and nothing measured this before: the ring is the brand hue, so it moved whenever the brand moved and was checked only by eye.

The focus indicator against the ink page. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of a focus ring, and nothing measured this before: the ring is the brand hue, so it moved whenever the brand moved and was checked only by eye.

The focus indicator against an elevated card. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of a focus ring, and nothing measured this before: the ring is the brand hue, so it moved whenever the brand moved and was checked only by eye.

Link text on an ink ground. C4 measures the brand blue on the page ground and stops there, because text.brand was a light-ground colour when C4 was written; the case studies render on ink, where that same blue is 3.79:1 and a link is body-sized text needing 4.5. text.brand-on-ink is the lifted rendition and this is what measures it (6.93:1). Role is fixed rather than reading: reading would derive a dark twin of a token that IS the dark twin. The pair exists because a rule setting only `color` states no background, so CV1 cannot see this one — it is the inherited-ground case in its own contract, and the answer to an invisible pair is to declare it here.

contrast.override_because: C1-C15 are deliberately exitless. A contrast ratio is the one thing in this contract a reader experiences directly, and an override would let a surface ship unreadable text with a reason attached. There is no reason that makes 3:1 body copy legible. The fix for a failing pair is the colour, never the clause.

color_space.$description: CS1. Perceptual ramps are declared in OKLCH. The neutral ramp, the brand pair and danger are the colours chosen by eye along a lightness or chroma progression, and OKLCH is the space that keeps those steps even; the fixed anchors (ink, paper, white, black and the alpha ladders) stay sRGB because they are exact values rather than points on a ramp. F3 already bounds which spaces the FORMAT permits — this states which space these tokens must actually use, which is a different claim and does not borrow F3 authority. Known reach, stated rather than implied: this proves every base colour under the listed prefixes declares oklch. It does not prove the ramps are perceptually uniform, that the steps are well chosen, or that an sRGB value declared elsewhere is not visually part of a ramp — a hex that happens to sit between two neutral steps is invisible to this and always will be. must_catch and must_never_catch are the C6 firing lists: samples run through the clause own predicate on every run, so a clause that has quietly stopped matching cannot report health it never established.

must_catch.why: a ramp colour demoted to sRGB is the defect this clause exists for
a single step leaving the space breaks the ramp evenness without breaking the build

must_never_catch.why: a fixed anchor is sRGB by design and outside the prefixes
the compliant case must not be flagged, or the clause fails closed on a healthy tree

hdr_ceiling.$description: CS2. No token's HDR rendition may render brighter than HDR Reference White. A token may carry an org.metis.hdr anchor, which build.mjs emits as color-hdr(<token> 0, <anchor> N) inside an @supports guard: the user agent interpolates between the two by the display's headroom, and never tells anyone what that headroom was. WHY A CEILING AND NOT A RATIO. Every C clause here measures a WCAG ratio, and WCAG is calibrated for a regime whose brightest white IS reference white — which is the definition of SDR (CSS Color HDR 1 s2.2: SDR has 0 stops of headroom). Above reference white there is no author-side criterion in any specification; the HDR module's entire Accessibility Considerations section asks the USER AGENT to offer a luminance limit and gives authors nothing to measure against. So the rule is a bound, not a ratio: stay inside the regime the ratios were defined for. Known reach, stated rather than implied: this proves that every DECLARED HDR anchor sits at or below the ceiling, and that the headroom-0 anchor is the ordinary token, so C1-C15 go on auditing exactly what an SDR display shows. It does not audit what renders BETWEEN the stops — that is interpolated by the user agent in Absolute D65 XYZ, is deliberately not exposed, and has no threshold defined for it by anyone. It also says nothing about HDR imagery or video, which carry their own luminance and are reached only by the reader's dynamic-range-limit control, not by this clause. ceiling_nits is the policy number and lives here; the 203 in tokens/hdr.mjs is a different quantity wearing the same value — the Yw unit conversion that turns xyz-d65 into Absolute D65 XYZ, which is physics from Rpt BT.2408-9 and belongs with the arithmetic. must_catch and must_never_catch are the C6 firing lists, run through the clause's own predicate on every run. Source: CSS Color HDR Module Level 1, W3C Working Draft 28 July 2026; a Working Draft, and tokens/decisions.md carries the caveat on building against one.

must_catch.why: the spec's own blinding white, 10000 cd/m2, displayable only briefly on a small area; if this stops being caught the clause has stopped meaning anything
one percent over reference white must fail, or the bound is decorative rather than enforced
HLG's white luminance depends on viewing conditions, so no ceiling is checkable from the declaration; refusing it is the honest outcome and scoring it as zero would be the dangerous one

must_never_catch.why: exactly reference white is the boundary the rule admits: may not EXCEED, so equality passes
the shipped brand anchor at 33.3 cd/m2 — the compliant case must not be flagged, or the clause fails closed on a healthy tree
an SDR colour cannot exceed reference white by definition, so the clause must have nothing to say about one

hdr_ceiling.override_because: CS2 is deliberately exitless. Above HDR Reference White no specification gives an author a criterion, so an override would be a waiver against no standard at all -- a reason with nothing to be reasonable about. The fix is the anchor.

contrast_coverage.$description: contract.md CV1 (decision R-71). C1-C15 prove the ratio of every pair someone declared; this proves nobody is rendering a pair they forgot to declare. It reads the surfaces for a rule that sets BOTH a foreground and a background from tokens, resolves each through cssName and the alias map (so --ame-text-body is measured as text.body in light and text.body-on-dark in dark), and requires the resulting pair to be one checkContrast already measured. Pair order is normalized because the WCAG ratio is symmetric: background.page on text.brand is C4 read backwards, not a new pair. The fix for a violation is to add the pair to contrast.pairs, which puts it under C-clause measurement automatically — so this clause proves coverage and the C clauses prove ratios, one home each. Known reach, stated rather than implied: it only sees a foreground and background stated in the SAME rule or the same inline style object. A background set on a container with the colour inherited by a child is a real rendered pair this cannot see, so a pass means no DECLARABLE pair was missed, not that every rendered pair is covered. Alpha fills are composited over the surface's declared ground before measuring: a translucent background states its pigment, not the colour anyone reads, so the pair that carries the requirement is the foreground against the ground beneath, which contrast.darkGround holds one per theme. A C clause measuring fg-on-ground therefore covers a surface painting that fg on a fill above it; the compositing itself is contrast.mjs, proven both ways in tests/tokens.test.ts (a fill that only passes once composited, and one that still fails after).
contrast_coverage.waived_because: Empty: every co-located pair the scan resolves today is already declared. An entry needs a dated decision naming why a rendered pair legitimately carries no contrast requirement — decorative text over an image, or a foreground the design intends to be invisible.

parity.$description: P1 to P3. A value with a second home in hand-written source. The token is the home; the literal must equal it. Each entry names the file, the pattern that finds the literal, and the token it must match.

duplication.$description: D1. A generated custom property re-declared in hand-written CSS is a second home for one value. Exceptions are values the token layer cannot hold: a runtime-switched assignment, or an asset.

allowed_because.--port-glass-fg: Runtime-switched between two tokens by [data-backdrop]. The values are tokens; only the assignment is CSS.
allowed_because.--port-glass-halo: A text-shadow the design sets to none on every surface. No second value exists to hold.
allowed_because.--ame-component-accessibility-width: The base width is component.accessibility.width; the >=768px override is a calc() over the grid, which has no token form.
allowed_because.--ask-w: A local alias inside the anchor's centring math. Reads --ame-component-accessibility-width; holds nothing.

restated.$description: D2. D1 catches a re-declared custom property. It cannot see a hand-written literal that happens to equal a token's resolved value, which is the same second home wearing different syntax: the nav pill and the work card each restated a shadow recipe the token layer already held, and the gate passed. Compared by numeric signature (the ordered numbers in the value) so rgba(16,19,25, 0.04) and rgb(16 19 25 / 0.04) are recognised as one value. min_numbers keeps single scalars from matching everything.

shipped.$description: G1. A placeholder that survives into emitted HTML says on its face that the page is unfinished, so it must never reach a deployed route. Evaluated only in --shipped mode, after next build, against the emitted app tree. STANDARD.md C5 is the same condition at repo scope; this is its one evaluation site.
shipped.$pattern_note: A bare \[\[ also matches React Server Component payload nesting (`[[["",{"children"`), which every Next 16 route emits, so it flagged 40+ routes that hold no placeholder. The pattern requires a bracketed identifier, which is the shape the source placeholders actually use ([[META_DESCRIPTION]], [[year]]). STANDARD.md C5's own grep is the untightened form; this is its one evaluation site and the tightening is decision D-15.
shipped.override_because: G1 is deliberately exitless. A placeholder that reaches a rendered route is unfinished work presented as fact, and an exemption would be a way to ship exactly that. What is unfinished is omitted or the build stops; there is no third state.

scales.$description: S1 to S5. Every literal of a scaled kind found in portfolio source must be a member of that scale. Reported as drift with a baseline rather than as a hard failure: Tailwind arbitrary-value classes can introduce a literal without touching this directory, so the count is a measurement that must not grow, in the shape CLAUDE.md uses for duplication.

entries.$description: S6. A FRACTIONAL opacity literal is a design decision and must be a member of the opacity scale. 0 and 1 are excluded by the pattern rather than by an exception list: they are the identity values, fully transparent and fully opaque, which no scale owns and which appeared 44 times in this surface as plain structural facts. Matching only 0.x keeps the clause on the values someone chose. The matcher is ASSEMBLED IN CODE from the literal property name above, not typed here as a regex: D3 holds pattern syntax out of rule data, and S1-S5 predate that rule rather than licensing more of it. property is literal text; fractional_only says 0 and 1 are outside the clause.

S7. A line-height literal must be a member of the leading ramp. The ramp existed in the token layer from the beginning and nothing held anything to it: the census covered font.size, unit, radius, duration, z and opacity, so leading was the one scale with a ramp and no clause, and values sat off it unseen. Found by converting arbitrary Tailwind values into token references -- 1.6 and 1.5 turned out to be real ramp members while 1.45, 1.3 and 1.1 were on no scale at all. NOT fractional_only, unlike S6: a leading value is a ratio above 1, so the 0.x pattern that keeps identity values out of the opacity clause would match none of these. The matcher is assembled in code from the literal property name (D3 keeps regex out of rule data). Known reach, stated rather than implied: this reads the Tailwind utility form, `leading-[N]`, and the CSS-property form. There are no inline lineHeight literals in the scanned surfaces today, so nothing is currently lost to that gap, but a value written as a style-object lineHeight would pass unseen.

S8. A letter-spacing literal must be a member of the tracking ramp. Ramped and unwatched until this pass: the ramp shipped with the token layer and nothing counted strays against it, which is the same shape as S7's leading gap. Declared in coverage.ramped, which is what forced it — Z5 fails a ramp with no clause.

S9. A px spacing literal must be a member of the unit ramp. S2 watches the same ramp in rem only, so every px padding, margin and gap sat outside the census. `properties` lists the utilities that write to this ramp rather than matching any property: a property-agnostic px pattern would swallow text-[14px] and max-w-[760px] too, turning a spacing clause into a census of everything on the page.

S10. A backdrop-blur literal must be a member of the glass ramp. The smallest possible drift, and the clearest exhibit in the repo: glass.blur holds 14px, four surfaces write backdrop-blur-[14px], and until this clause nothing sat between them. One token, four matching literals, no connection.

S11. An arbitrary responsive variant must name a breakpoint the ramp holds. Tailwind's min-[1320px] syntax creates a breakpoint inline, which is a design decision written where no one reviews it, against a ramp that already declares the two this system uses.

S12. An easing curve must be a member of the ease ramp. The one scale the generic matcher cannot read: its members are four-number curves, so membership is a tuple comparison and it gets its own branch in check.mjs. Ramped and unwatched until this pass, like tracking and leading before it — the ramp existed and nothing counted strays against it. The clause COUNTS; it does not decide what the strays are. Whether an off-ramp curve is a candidate step or drift is a separate call, and a fresh non-zero count is exactly the moment that call is most likely to be made badly.

binding.$description: U1. The deliverable standard's allowed binding paths, as a tripwire. Surfaces bind semantic and component tokens; only tokens bind base tokens. A surface reading a base custom property resolves fine by name and violates the layering the deliverable list publishes, so the gate and the deliverable list agree by construction. The base-name set is derived from the token tree at check time, never restated here or in check.mjs. Aliases are not base names: an alias is a spelling the surface is meant to bind. Known reach, stated rather than implied: this proves no scanned file contains a literal base-name reference, not that no surface reaches a primitive. A 0 is produced equally by a clean tree and by a scan with nothing to find — a surface path that exists but holds no var() at all reads 0 and passes, as does a var() composed at runtime or a base name spelled through a variable. Z3 closes the missing-path half; the rest is closed by mutation rather than by counting, which is the next thing to build. Read the count as no literal base-name reference was found IN WHAT WAS SCANNED, and treat surfaces as part of the claim.
binding.surfaces_because: U1 always read .ts and .tsx, but only under the two portfolio directories, so the /ame area was a surface the tripwire did not watch. It bound five base primitives through inline style: --ame-color-ink, --ame-radius-pill, --ame-duration-slow, --ame-font-size-13 (nav.tsx) and --ame-font-leading-relaxed (footer.tsx). Each was repointed at the role that already held its value, and the two roles that did not exist yet were added (type.body-leading, component.nav.pill-fg), so the count is 0 across the widened scope and needed no baseline. Two directories stay out and are named rather than silently absent: components/ui is vendored and its names are upstream's call (R-8), and app/prototypes renders outside the token scope on purpose, binding its own --ambient-* namespace (R-66).
binding.exclude_because: U1 scans source text, and it cannot tell a binding from a QUOTATION of one. This page documents the rule by showing the violation next to the legal form — a `Don't` code sample reading var(--ame-font-size-13) — so the scanner counted the counter-example as the thing it warns against. The exclusion is the narrowest available: whole-file, because exclude matches paths, which is the cost. What it gives up is U1 cover over this file's real inline bindings, all of which are semantic today (--ame-text-secondary and friends). A token-aware MDX rule — skip fenced code, scan the JSX — would make the exclusion unnecessary and is the fix if a second page ever needs this.

uses_graph.$description: U2 to U4. The Parnas acyclic, layered uses-graph, extended off the portfolio surface that U1 already guards. The base-name set is DERIVED from the token tree at check time (the base tier names itself), never a prefix list: base and semantic share first segments (--border, --font, --duration each appear in BOTH tiers), so a prefix would misclassify a semantic token as base. Vendored components/ui is out of scope (R-8), the portfolio surface is U1's, and the emitted token CSS is the supplier, not a consumer. Source: STANDARD.md M (Parnas 1972, the acyclic uses-graph); DECISIONS R-26.

base_read.$description: No file in the app/components tree reads a base-tier custom property. U1 is this rule on the portfolio surface; U2 is the same rule on the rest of the tree (the /system shell and the shared ame chrome). Base binds base; a surface binds semantic or component.
base_read.waived_because: components/ame/* are the shared chrome (AmeNav, AmeFooter; R-12), tone-portable across the portfolio and the metis-marketing sister ground. Repointing these five base reads onto semantic or component roles is a scoped change: each replacement must resolve on BOTH grounds, and the marketing site syncs the generated CSS, so the repoint is a consumer migration owed to a dedicated order, not this check-adding pass (CLAUDE.md 9, the honest deferral). U2 waives the five known reads by name and blocks a sixth from landing. Follow-up: a dedicated order repoints components/ame off base and removes these waivers.

lib_no_app.$description: No lib/ module imports from app/. lib sits below app in the layered uses-graph, so a lib->app edge would make the graph cyclic. Matches @/app, @/app/*, and relative ../app paths.

surface_no_system_tokens.$description: No portfolio surface imports a lib/*-tokens design-token module. The portfolio DTOS token system and the lib/*-tokens /system design system are two homes for 'design tokens', adjudicated as two concepts in DECISIONS R-25. A portfolio-surface import of a lib/*-tokens module would merge them into a hidden third binding; this keeps the two concepts two.

clients.$description: H1. A token nothing consumes is a clause with one signature. A client is: a var() in portfolio source, another token's reference, an alias, or a named invariant that reads the token. The count of clientless tokens is a measurement, recorded in outcomes.md, and must not grow. The compiled recipe stylesheet (clients.generated) is a client too: it is what consumes a recipe token by name.

invariant_clients.$description: Tokens whose client is an invariant rather than a call site. A closed scale is consumed whole by the check that admits nothing outside it.
invariant_clients.dither: derived:--ame-dither-noise (build.mjs serializes frequency and octaves into the feTurbulence URI)

lint.$description: Code-quality thresholds for eslint.config.mjs (WO-6.1, decision R-23, superseding tokens/decisions.md D-12). This file is the one home for the numbers; eslint.config.mjs reads them with readFileSync so the config states no threshold of its own, the same relation deliverables.md sets for the gate. Evaluated by ESLint, not check.mjs. `complexity` is an ERROR set at the current measured cyclomatic maximum, so it is green now and only ever ratchets DOWN as deep functions are split. The three max_* entries are WARNING thresholds; their counts are baselined in tokens/lint-baseline.json under the same move-down-only rule as baseline.json (X1). max_params is 6, STANDARD.md M2's stated limit, so a seventh parameter warns.

structured_data.$description: STANDARD.md D5 (WO-7.4, decision R-30). The data for the JSON-LD entity-graph checks. Evaluated by tests/json-ld.test.tsx, not check.mjs, the same way `lint` is evaluated by ESLint: this file is the one home for the values, the checker reads them. The blacklist is superseded/replaced Schema.org properties that must never appear in an emitted node; every property maps to its live replacement, which the check names when it fails. proficiency_levels is the closed vocabulary a TechArticle's proficiencyLevel may draw from.

ame_taxonomy.$description: contract.md AM2 (DECISIONS R-55, R-57, R-65). The five docs tiers of the /ame brand design system (Foundations, Layouts, Components, Sections, Pages), disjoint from the /system taxonomy (`taxonomy` above). content/ame/meta.json is the one home for which page sits in which tier; this lists the tiers and, for a deliberately deferred tier, the recorded reason. AM2 in check.mjs (checkAmeTaxonomyRegistry) holds every declared tier non-empty (at least one page under its separator in meta.json) or carrying a deferred_because here, so a tier is never silently absent. A sub-group separator inside a tier (Lockups, Header, Footer) is a visual grouping in meta.json, not a declared tier; AM2 only requires the tiers listed here, so an extra separator is admitted and ignored (R-65 M5). tiers also supplies the valid-tier set AM1 checks a registry row's tier against. The developer-facing get-started (formerly the 'For developers' tier, R-65 M4) is now the /ame index page itself; the tier is retired and its binding steps live in the index.

ame_registry.$description: contract.md AM1, AM3 (DECISIONS R-57). The /ame brand registry as the single home the /ame docs and gate checks read, parallel to and disjoint from `registry` (the /system registry; no component in both, clause H). Rows live in content/ame/component-registry.json. AM1 (checkAmeTaxonomyRegistry): every .tsx file under scan_dirs, minus the excluded set, has exactly one registry row keyed by source, that row points at a real file, and its tier is one of ame_taxonomy.tiers; a row may also point at a file outside scan_dirs (the viewer under extra_note) as long as it resolves and carries a valid tier. AM3: every row with animated true AND status equal to playground_status ('documented') must name a `playground` field resolving to an existing file; this session every animated row is status 'deferred', so AM3 passes vacuously and binds in Phase 3. excluded is the exemption set: context providers and pure-logic sinks that are not documentable UI, named with the reason, the same shape as the vendored-ui exemption (registry's components/ui scope note).
ame_registry.extra_note: components/prototype-viewer/viewer.tsx carries a row too (the prototype viewer) though it sits outside scan_dirs; AM1 admits a row whose source resolves and whose tier is valid, so the viewer row passes without being part of the mandatory coverage scan.

excluded.components/portfolio/privacy-facts.tsx: ControllerAddress / LogRetention — two components that each render one string from lib/portfolio/privacy, for the same reason ContactEmail beside them does: the GDPR requires the policy to carry these disclosures, and MDX copy cannot follow a module when that module changes. They render text and nothing else, with no element and no styling of their own, so there is no surface to document and nothing a playground could vary. A catalog entry would document an address and a retention period rather than a component.
excluded.components/portfolio/cookie-consent.tsx: CookieConsent — DEFERRED. Its only consumers are the docs machinery itself (mount.tsx, playground-embed and its own playground); no site surface renders it, because this site sets no cookies and shows no banner, which the privacy policy states as a positive claim. So the page documented an interaction the site does not have, using two unfilled category descriptions. RESTORE if the site ever needs consent, at which point the descriptions are content someone has to write anyway.
excluded.components/portfolio/outcome-section.tsx: OutcomeSection — DEFERRED, not excluded on principle. Its own header records that this section carried another person's project data (CC Scripts: sales, visitors, bounce), which was purged and replaced with placeholder tokens so the structure could be kept while the numbers could not. Nothing mounts it; its only appearance was the catalog page, which published STAT_1 through STAT_3 and TRACK_RECORD on a reachable route. Documenting an unwritten section is the same defect as publishing an unwritten case study. RESTORE when real, verified numbers exist to put in it — the row and its page regenerate from this file.
excluded.components/portfolio/scaffold-sections.t: ScaffoldSections — DEFERRED for the same reason. Covenants, the first-90-days note, the how-to-read note and the contact intro were never written, so the catalog page shipped seven placeholder tokens. Nothing mounts it. RESTORE when the copy exists.
excluded.components/portfolio/slide-gallery.tsx: SlideGallery — DEFERRED. Its only consumer is its own playground, and its key-media default was never filled, so the catalog page published CASE_n_KEY_MEDIA. RESTORE when a surface uses it and the default names real media.
excluded.components/portfolio/contact-email.tsx: ContactEmail — the owner's address, rendered so prose can state it without typing it. It exists because Article 13(1)(a) makes the privacy policy's contact detail a legal requirement rather than a link, and MDX copy cannot follow lib/portfolio/contact.ts when that changes. What it renders is one string from that module: there is no surface to document and nothing a playground could vary, and a catalog entry would document the address rather than a component.
excluded.components/portfolio/shimmer-sweep.tsx: ShimmerSweep — the clock for the hero CTA's shimmer, and only the clock. The look is .port-shimmer in portfolio.css, which owns the mask, the glow stacks and the upstream licence; this drives its timeline and renders no box of its own. Documenting it would put the appearance on a page that does not define it, which is the drift AM1 exists to stop rather than a row it should hold.
excluded.components/portfolio/sync-card-loop.tsx: SyncCardLoop — a loop driver around components/ui/sync-card. SyncCard plays once and exposes play/reset on a handle; this adds the repeat and nothing visual. The surface belongs to SyncCard, which sits in components/ui and is outside these scan_dirs by R-8, so a row here would be a catalog entry for timing attached to a component the catalog does not hold.
excluded.components/portfolio/portfolio-theme.tsx: PortfolioThemeProvider / usePortfolioTheme — a React context provider and its hook, not a rendered UI component. It supplies theme state to the tree; there is no visual surface to document or give a playground.
excluded.components/portfolio/a11y-prefs.tsx: PortfolioA11yProvider / usePortfolioA11y and A11Y_DEFAULTS — a React context provider, its hook, and its default record. State plumbing, not a documentable surface (the visible accessibility UI is portfolio-accessibility.tsx, which carries its own row).
excluded.components/portfolio/session-activity.ts: PortfolioSessionActivity — a pure side-effect sink that returns null (a useEffect logging session activity). It renders nothing, so it is not a documentable UI component.
excluded.components/ame/icons/icon-fallback.tsx: IconFallback — the client-only lucide fallback branch of the Icon primitive (components/ame/icons/icon.tsx, which carries the row). Split out so Icon stays server-renderable; it renders only through Icon and has no standalone surface to document.

ame_registry.excluded_because: Three files under the scan dirs are not documentable brand components: two are context providers and one is a render-null side-effect sink. Documenting them would assert a UI surface where there is none, the inverse of the frontier-stub disclosure rule (CLAUDE.md 12). Each is named here with its reason, the same exemption pattern registry gives vendored components/ui. A fourth file added under the scan dirs that is a real component gets a row or fails AM1; adding a provider here is a deliberate, recorded act.

asset_budget.$description: contract.md K1 (WO-8.6, decision R-40). A per-class byte ceiling on everything under public/, so the 25 MB-SVG / 82 MB-GLB class of regression cannot land silently again. A file is classed by its extension; the classes and their byte ceilings are `budgets`. A file over its class ceiling is a K1 VIOLATION, not drift: it is a stated ceiling, not a count that may creep to a baseline. `waived` is the ratchet for assets that already exceed their ceiling and cannot be reduced in this check-adding pass; each names its current byte size and is owned by a reduction order (see waived_because). A waived file passes while it does not GROW past the recorded size, so the ratchet only ever moves down, the same rule X1 gives drift counts. Extensions outside every class (.html) are not assets this clause weighs. Sizes are the REAL object's bytes. When the bytes on disk are a Git LFS pointer, the size is read from the pointer's own size line rather than from the ~130-byte stub; weighing the stub said an 83MB model was 130 bytes and under budget, which was true about what was present and useless as a guarantee, and it made the verdict depend on whether the checkout smudged. Reading the pointer makes K1 byte-exact on any checkout, which is what lets both workflows set lfs: false and stop fetching the objects at all. Only files small enough to be a pointer are opened, and a pointer with no size line fails rather than falling back to the stub's length.
asset_budget.budgets_because: svg 500 KB matches WO-8.1's stated re-authoring target for the Kindle SVGs; the real vector SVGs in the tree top out at 59 KB (logo/lockup.svg). font 500 KB clears the two InterVariable variable woff2 files (~388 KB, legitimately larger for two axes) and the InterDisplay/NeueHaas cuts (~110 KB) while blocking a return of the ~900 KB TTF class. image 250 KB clears the endorsement thumbnails (152 KB) and avatars (~100 KB) and catches the one ~0.9 MB art cover. model 5 MB is the repo's V4 large-binary sensibility and a realistic DRACO-compressed GLB target, against the 82.7 MB uncompressed model.

asset_budget.waived_because: TWO SHAPES, AND THE NEWER ONE IS THE SPEC. A waiver may be a plain byte count -- the ten legacy entries, held at their current size by the ratchet under the shared reduction order below -- or an object stating clause, ceiling, measured bytes, owner, date recorded, reduction target, the reduction itself and the trigger that ends it. New waivers take the object form. The difference between a waiver and a bypass is specification: a bypass says the check does not apply, a waiver says what it measured, what that exceeds, who owns closing it and when. The legacy ten keep their numbers rather than being given invented owners and dates, because a fabricated provenance is worse than an honest count. Waived assets are REPORTED, never silent: check.mjs prints a WAIVED block and the run's verdict carries the count, so a clean run reads PASS+2W rather than PASS. Ten assets exceed their class ceiling today and are held at their current byte size by the ratchet until a dedicated reduction order shrinks them (CLAUDE.md 9, the honest deferral). kindle-mascot.svg (10.0 MB) and kindle-ux-collection.svg (15.0 MB) are almost certainly embedded raster in an SVG wrapper; re-authoring them to <=500 KB each is WO-8.1, and that outcome is what unblocks Agent 3 WO-3.2 (the V4 large-binary breach). iphone17-pro.glb (82.7 MB) waits on a DRACO/meshopt-compressed variant plus viewer lazy-load (WO-8.1, WO-8.5). frieren-manga.jpg (0.9 MB) waits on image optimization and the WO-8.7 display-size resize. screens/6-10.svg (3.8-8.1 MB) are the Kindle Japan product screens feeding the case-study PanelWall hero: embedded raster in an SVG wrapper, they wait on a raster re-export (WebP/PNG) that both clears the ceiling and cuts the wall's ~15-20s first-paint. screens/activating.svg (0.6 MB) is the same family (the Activating-state screen, exact source bytes kept unminified so the render is identical to the design file) and waits on the same raster re-export. Each waiver may not grow: a larger re-export fails K1, so the ratchet only ever moves down.

workflows.$description: STANDARD.md section W (decision R-69). A path spelled inside a CI step is a binding like any other, and until now it was the only binding in this repo that nothing verified. The break it closes, found on this branch: both workflows ran `node tokens/build.mjs` for the whole life of a branch that had already moved that script to packages/ame-tokens/build.mjs. Nothing went red, because the workflows had never been pushed and so had never run — the same vacuous pass V7 has while no tag exists. W1 verifies every script path and script name a workflow or a package.json script spells, against the tree, at gate time instead of at first-push time. W2 asserts each workflow declares a least-privilege token. Data here, logic in checkWorkflows in check.mjs, clause in STANDARD.md section W.
workflows.runner_builtins_because: A runner's own subcommand is not a package.json script; `pnpm install` must not be read as a missing script. A name is checked against scripts first, so a builtin that is also a script here (test, start) is still verified as the script it is.
workflows.banned_version_keys_because: A runtime version written into a workflow is a version with as many homes as there are workflows. It was spelled `node-version: 24` in both of this repo's jobs, which could drift onto different runtimes with neither file looking wrong — while the pnpm comment three lines above explained why pnpm's version is read from package.json instead. The -file form gives the version one home that CI and a local nvm/fnm both read. W1 verifies the file that form points at actually exists, so the indirection cannot become a dangling reference.
workflows.ignore_because: No referenced path is exempt today. An entry here needs a dated decision naming why a path a CI step spells legitimately does not exist in the tree — a file an earlier step generates before use is the one plausible case.
workflows.uninvoked_because: W1 checks that every script a workflow NAMES resolves to the tree. W3 is its mirror: that every script the manifest DEFINES is named by something. The gap between them is where a check can exist, be correct, and never run — docgen once (CI omitted a step pnpm build had always run) and typecheck again (defined before the workflow existed, invoked by nothing, four errors accumulated behind it, R-136/R-138). The defect is invisible precisely because the script passes whenever a human happens to run it by hand, so only a comparison can see it. An exemption is data with a stated reason, per R-82: a script may legitimately have no in-repo caller, but it may not have no answer.

uninvoked_exempt.dev: developer rite: the local server, run by a person at a keyboard and by nothing else.
uninvoked_exempt.start: developer rite: serves an already-built tree locally. The deploy platform runs its own start.
uninvoked_exempt.build: invoked by the deploy platform outside this repo, which is why CI runs the chain step by step rather than calling it. The one script whose caller is real but not in the tree.
uninvoked_exempt.ame: the dipstick rite (LEXICON: dipstick). Read-only and deliberately hand-run, so a dated export is a decision someone made rather than a file CI rewrites.
uninvoked_exempt.docgen: the writing half of docgen:check, run by hand when generated docs must be regenerated. The checking half is what the gate needs, and it is wired.
uninvoked_exempt.diagram: The writer half of the README diagram. CI runs diagram:check; this one is run by a person when the tokens move, the same relationship tokens:build has to the gate.
uninvoked_exempt.numbers: The writer half of the README figures. CI runs numbers:check; this one is run by a person after the tokens move, the same relationship diagram has to diagram:check.

vendored.$description: STANDARD.md section VN (decision R-72). Both this tree and the comparison tree it was measured against carry code their author did not write; only one recorded where it came from. components/ui holds 61 files copied from the shadcn/ui registry with no upstream revision, no manifest, and a blanket lint carve-out (R-8) standing in for a written boundary. VN1 holds VENDORED.md and the tree to each other by machine: every file under a root is listed, every listed path exists, so a component cannot be added without recording it. VN2 asserts the root has one home — the string components/ui is spelled in three enforcement places (eslint ignores, synonyms.symbol_exclude, uses_graph.exclude_prefixes), and a rename that missed one would silently un-exempt or over-exempt the directory. What VN1 cannot do is verify the files match upstream; that needs the revision the import never recorded, which VENDORED.md states as an open gap rather than inventing.

coverage.$description: THE DENOMINATOR. A grep for arbitrary Tailwind values in the scanned surfaces returns 172, and until this block existed nothing told the reader which of them were debt. The incumbent reading — all of it is debt — won by default, because it was the only reading available in four minutes. This declares the boundary so the cheap check and the gate answer the same question. `ramped` lists the properties that have a scale in the token layer and must therefore never carry a literal; `layout` lists the properties that deliberately have none. The second list is a stated non-goal with reasons, not an oversight, and saying so once is what stops every future reader re-discovering ~70 layout measures as debt. The claim this makes possible is ZERO LITERALS ON A RAMPED PROPERTY, which is checkable. It is deliberately not 'fully tokenized': that phrase invites a reader to include the layout measures and re-litigate the boundary, so the defined thing is claimed and the slogan is retired.
coverage.ramped_because: Each of these has a ramp in the token layer, so a literal is a value that left the scale rather than a measure with no scale to be on. FIVE NULL CLAUSES ARE THE HONEST PART: letter-spacing, easing, px spacing, backdrop-blur and breakpoint are ramped and UNWATCHED. A stray tracking value, an off-ramp cubic-bezier, a px padding, a hand-typed 14px blur where glass.blur already holds 14px, or a min-[1320px] variant against a real breakpoint ramp — all invisible to the census today. S2 watches spacing in rem only, which is why px spacing sits outside it. Recorded here rather than discovered later, because a completeness claim whose denominator is itself incomplete is the failure mode every clause added this session has demonstrated: leading had a ramp and no clause for the whole of its existence.
coverage.layout_because: These are MEASURES, not steps. A prose column at 760px is a reading-width decision answering to line length, not a member of a shared ramp, and there is no ratio that generates 760 from 720. Inventing a width scale so a sentence can say everything is tokenized would be the tail wagging the dog: it would add names nobody binds by role and make the taxonomy larger and less true. They stay literal, deliberately, and this line is the difference between deliberate and deferred.
coverage.appeal: A property moves from layout to ramped when the same value appears at 4 or more sites AND those sites share a role rather than only a number — the same test a new token must pass (decisions.md D-50). max-w-[760px] currently sits at 12 sites, so it clears the count and fails the role test: those sites share 'a readable column', which is one role, and that is a live candidate someone should file as a token proposal rather than a rule to hide behind. This boundary is authored by the party being measured, so it carries reasons and an exit; a list without either reads as gerrymandering and should.

census.$description: contract.md section Z (WO-9.1, decision R-50). The contract->invariants->check bijection, made machine-enforced instead of discipline-enforced. checkCensus parses the clause IDs declared in tokens/contract.md (the bold **A1** / **C1-C15** markers, en-dash normalized) and asserts each one has a census record below; a record names the invariants.json key that holds the clause's data (`invariant`) and the function in check.mjs that evaluates it (`check`), or carries a `structural` waiver naming the build.mjs mechanism that enforces it instead of a check.mjs branch. A clause with no record, a record naming a missing invariants key, or a record naming a check function absent from check.mjs fails Z1. A census record for a clause the contract no longer declares also fails, so the map cannot rot. threshold_scan is Z2: a grep-class scan asserting no threshold literal is hardcoded in the checker (deliverables.md: the gate imports its thresholds, never restates them), with a small allowlist of legitimate constants. Data here, logic in check.mjs, clause in contract.md, one home each.

A1.structural: build.mjs throws on a token missing $value before any check runs (contract.md: violating A1 stops the build). Reaching check.mjs proves it.

A4.structural: build.mjs (resolveValue) throws on an unresolved reference or a reference cycle before any check runs (contract.md: violating A4 stops the build).

B1.structural: build.mjs postcondition: each token is emitted exactly once under .portfolio-root. build.mjs is the single writer; a token cannot be emitted twice from one enumeration.

B2.structural: build.mjs postcondition: toCss serializes every value to a CSS literal; resolveValue leaves no {reference} unresolved, or A4 would have thrown.

B3.structural: build.mjs postcondition: each ALIASES entry emits var(--token) and throws if the alias does not resolve to exactly one token.

P1-P3.scope_because: parity against constants in this app's components

KW1.scope_because: the résumé keyword map is this app's claim surface

G1.scope_because: placeholders in the emitted app tree; the package emits no app

U4.scope_because: the boundary against a second token system this app once carried

X1.structural: the drift ratchet's data home is baseline.json and runs.log, not invariants.json; checkRecord evaluates a baseline against the last logged run, so X1 has a check but no invariants entry by design.

AM1.scope_because: the /ame docs registry is this app's catalog

AM2.scope_because: the /ame docs tiers are this app's information architecture

AM3.scope_because: the /ame docs registry is this app's catalog

K1.scope_because: a byte ceiling over public/, which the package does not have

U5.scope_because: which stylesheet loads on which route is this app's routing

RC1.scope_because: a recipe names an element, and the elements are this app's components

FX1.structural: Enforced from outside this file on purpose. check.mjs --fixtures only widens a scan list; tokens/gate-fixtures.mjs runs it and inverts the verdict, so the gate itself has no mode in which failing is success. A checkFixtures() in here would be that mode.

LC1.scope_because: the licence travels with the package and is the first thing a stranger reads

allowlists.$description: Z4. Every allowlisted exception in the census names its reason, and the total number of them is a ratcheted measurement. An allowlist is where a clause admits it cannot judge something, which makes it the cheapest way to silence a failing check and the place drift hides in plain sight. Two conditions: an entry must carry a non-empty reason, so it cannot be anonymous and cannot be retired without someone having said what it bought; and the count of entries across every census allowlist is recorded as drift, so baseline.json holds it to the same one-way constraint as every other measured number — the lists may be emptied, never extended. Allowlists are located by SHAPE, any census key named `allow` or `allow_something`, rather than by a registry an author would have to remember to join. Known reach, stated rather than implied: this covers the census's own allowlists, not the exemption lists elsewhere in this file (ame_registry.excluded, css_scope.exempt), which predate it and are counted by their own clauses.

denominator.$description: Z3. No clause measures over a denominator that is not there. A check whose scan root does not exist reads zero files, finds zero violations, and passes — reporting a health nothing established. RC1 guards its own empty set by hand, which is the right instinct in one place: a guard every clause author must remember is discipline moved from the rule-follower to the rule-writer, not removed. So the record is kept in walkFiles, the primitive all sixteen scanning clauses reach through, and asserted here for every clause at once including the ones not written yet. Known reach, stated rather than implied: this proves a scan root EXISTS, not that it contains anything a clause can act on — an empty but present directory still yields a zero. The stronger form is a per-clause candidate count the census requires each clause to record, which is the version to build if a zero ever gets through this one. allow_missing names a path that is legitimately absent, with the reason; it is empty because none currently are.

threshold_scan.$description: Z2. No threshold literal hardcoded in check.mjs. The scan strips comments, strings, and regex literals, then flags any decimal literal or any integer >= min_integer that is not allowlisted. A threshold a clause compares against (a contrast minimum, a byte ceiling) lives in invariants.json; the checker reads it, never restates it. allow names the legitimate non-threshold constants that remain in checker code, each with its reason.

allow.120: display truncation length for a violation message (slice(0, 120))
allow.1000: seconds-to-milliseconds unit conversion in checkScales convert()

census.override_because: Z1 and Z2 are deliberately exitless. They are the clauses that hold the contract to its own shape -- a bijection with an exception is not a bijection, and a threshold scan that can be waived is a threshold scan the checker may quietly reacquire. A meta-clause with an override does not constrain anything.

pattern_escapes.$description: D3, the migration ratchet for R-86. Counts strings in each site whose parsed value carries a backslash — keys and values alike. The unit is the string, not the character: one stored pattern costs one whether it holds one escape or six, so rewriting a pattern with fewer escapes cannot look like progress. The rule these sites migrate toward is that rule data holds literal text and pattern syntax is assembled in code, where the escapes exist once and are tested (R-86). A file that has completed the migration measures zero.
pattern_escapes.sites_because: tokens/invariants.json is the one rule-data file that still carries pattern syntax; tokens/check.mjs feeds its values to new RegExp in six places. The escapes there are hand-maintained and have never been round-tripped through a serializer, so the risk is latent rather than active, which is why they are ratcheted rather than swept. Adding a site is how another file joins the migration.

css_scope.$description: U5. Definition scope must cover reference scope. A var() in a globally-loaded stylesheet whose custom property is defined only in a provincially-loaded one resolves to nothing on the routes the defining sheet does not reach, and CSS drops the declaration silently. Caught by hand at R-140 while reading the import graph for the WS-2 ratification, before any edit: @theme loads globally, --ame-unit-1 was emitted into a sheet only the portfolio route group imports. Data here, logic in checkCssScope in check.mjs, clause in tokens/contract.md.
css_scope.exempt_because: An exemption states that a var read globally but defined provincially is intended — a value that is meant to be absent outside its subtree and whose absence is handled. It is data with a reason, per R-82, and empty today because no such case exists.
css_scope.judged_scope_because: Only custom properties this repo defines somewhere are judged. One defined by Tailwind or fumadocs and read here is that dependency's to scope, and flagging it would bury the real finding in noise. The check therefore asks a narrow question it can answer: of the vars we own, is any of them read more widely than it is defined?

recipes.$description: RC1, RC2, RC3. A recipe is one component styling contract: slots, and the axes those slots vary along. The axes are DTCG Resolver 2025.10 modifiers, their contexts the values an axis takes, so the variant model is the standard one rather than this repo inventing a second. RC1 holds the recipe token grammar and the structural declarations honest, RC2 holds the resolver document to the spec, RC3 holds the component to the generated types so a variant cannot be a loose string again.

reachability.$description: H2 (STANDARD.md). Every source file is reachable from an entry point: a route file, a config, a test, or a content file, following imports transitively. Reachability is computed from the roots outward rather than by asking whether a file is MENTIONED anywhere, because two dead files that import each other mention each other and would keep one another alive forever. A file nothing reaches is dead code, and the standard says to delete it or record why it stays.

exempt.components/portfolio/case-study/chrome.t: Frame, ReturnContactBar, SectionMinimap, PageFooter and three shared class constants -- the chrome for long-form article pages from before the case studies and the privacy policy became MDX rendered through fumadocs. Held rather than deleted so its retirement is decided on its own terms instead of as a side effect of clearing a gate under deploy pressure. It ships nothing -- an unimported module is not in the bundle -- so the cost of holding it is this line. RETIREMENT TRIGGER: delete it, with anything that documents it, when the next long-form page type is authored and does not want it back; if a third one does want it, wire it up and this entry goes instead.

keywords.$description: KW1. The résumé grid's keywords and the evidence each linked one points at. The map is lib/portfolio/keywords.json and is the single home; keywords.ts is its typed view (the split-data-and-view shape of R-37). This entry names the files, never a keyword, a route, or a phrase. The check resolves every declared link against the file it names — a <Kw id> wrapper whose inner text must contain the declared evidence, or a heading that must exist in a generated page — and fails when an anchor is missing, when the evidence has moved out of it, or when a <Kw> in content is claimed by no keyword. A keyword with no example carries no link and is not this clause's business; KW1 governs the links that exist. Source: contract.md section KW.

package_manifest.$description: The paths that constitute the published package. The extraction script copies exactly these; the gate, run with --scope package, treats a scan root outside them as out of scope rather than absent. Both read this list, so what travels and what is checked cannot drift apart. Adding a path here is how a directory joins the package.
package_manifest.$workflow: The CI workflow is written by tokens/extract.mjs rather than copied. The monorepo workflow names scripts the package does not have (docgen, woven, the shipped check over an app tree it has none of), and W1 would rightly fail on every one. Generating it keeps the steps and the scripts in one hand.
package_manifest.$fixtures: examples/ and tokens/gate-fixtures.mjs travel: a gate nobody has watched fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot, and that argument is the package's to make as much as this repo's.
package_manifest.$closure: The manifest names an import closure, not a wish list. components/ame binds lib/a11y-glyph.ts and lib/translate.ts; leaving either out ships a package that cannot typecheck, which the CI sequence catches and a hand-check does not.

paratext.$description: Files the package publishes under a different name than they carry here, because this repo already has a README of its own. Source on the left, destination in the package on the right. They live in this repo so the extraction OWNS them: the published README said 264 tokens over a tree holding 339 precisely because it lived only in the published repo, where nothing here could check it.

fixtures.$description: The disconfirming world, as data. examples/compliant is inside the real gate's scan surfaces and carries the same obligations as application code; examples/violating is not, and is put in scope only by `node tokens/check.mjs --fixtures`, which tokens/gate-fixtures.mjs runs and then inverts. `scan_extends` names the clause scan lists the violating fixture joins, by invariants path, so the fixture's scope is stated once here instead of once per clause. `expect` is the claim the fixture makes about the gate: these clauses, and no fewer, must fire on it. A gate that stops catching one of them turns the fixture run red, which is the only way a regression in the gate itself becomes visible.

expect.$description: violations are clause ids that must appear under VIOLATIONS; drift_grows are measured counts that must exceed their baseline. Together they are the fixture's own postcondition.

fixtures.$extends_because: Two lists because the clauses read their roots two ways. A walker takes a directory and descends it; D1 and D2 open a stylesheet and read it. Handing a directory to the second is how the first attempt at this failed, so which list an entry belongs to is declared rather than guessed from its shape.

licence.$description: ONE LICENCE, SEVEN DECLARATIONS. The SPDX identifier below is the licence; every file listed under declarations must state it, and the check reads each one rather than trusting that a relicence remembered them all. This exists because the licence moved from MIT to Apache-2.0 on 2026-08-26 and the identifier was already written in seven places -- LICENSE, NOTICE, LICENSE-DOCS, CITATION.cff, the token package.json, the generated package.json in extract.mjs, and two READMEs. That is the same shape as the README figures that said 264 tokens over a tree holding 339: a fact restated by hand in many places, true when written, and false the moment one of them is missed. A licence is a worse thing to get wrong than a token count.
licence.$docs_because: The four prose documents are offered under either licence, at the recipient choice. LICENSE-DOCS names them and is the one home for that list.
licence.$forbidden_because: A stale MIT left anywhere in a live declaration is the exact failure this clause is for. Dated records -- CHANGELOG, DECISIONS.md, docs/orders, the preflight, tokens/decisions.md -- are history and correctly say MIT, so only the files named above are read. A line that names a declared third-party holder is exempt from the forbidden scan: NOTICE has to be able to say the icon set is MIT without that reading as a stale claim about this project. The exemption is narrow on purpose -- the holder must be named on the same line as the superseded identifier.

third_party.what: components/ame/icons/ — 218 glyphs generated from a Storybook export
must_contain: The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
third_party.$because: MIT is permissive but not unconditional: the permission notice must be included in all copies or substantial portions. 218 glyphs is a substantial portion. So the notice is not paperwork, it is the term that makes the use lawful, and it is checked rather than trusted to survive the next refactor. A link would not satisfy the condition; the text is reproduced.
